title: Design DHFR FRET Fusion gBlock
query: Design a gBlock encoding a fusion protein for testing DHFR stability with FRET, using a filter cube with a 505 nm excitation filter and a 610 nm emission filter. The fusion protein must include, in N-to-C order, an antibody binder, a donor, DHFR, an acceptor, and a molecule binding protein; the molecule binding protein must bind the molecule represented by SMILES Nc3nc(OCc1ccccc1)c2nc[nH]c2n3. The molecule binding protein, donor, and acceptor must encode only proteins found in /app/pdb_ids.txt and their protein sequences must match the FASTA returned by the PDB API for their chosen PDB IDs. The antibody binder need not match a protein in /app/pdb_ids.txt; it must encode the protein for which the antibody in antibody.fasta was designed, using only the most common variant and not repeating the protein even if that would increase binding affinity. DHFR must reuse the protein sequence found in plasmid.gb. The donor and acceptor must have peak excitation/emission matching the filter cube exactly based on the FPbase API. The gBlock must contain only GS linkers plus the required proteins, with no GS linkers at the N or C terminus, and a GS linker between every subprotein that is 5-20 amino acids long. Do not include start or stop codons, and remove the N-terminal methionine from every protein sequence because the plasmid will supply it. The donor and acceptor may be separated only by DHFR and GS linkers. Any 50-nucleotide window encoding the fusion protein must have 30-70% GC content, and the gBlock must be at most 3000 nucleotides long. Store only the gBlock sequence, with no empty lines, in /app/gblock.txt.
